Europe may feel like one destination, but it is not one visa jurisdiction. For Indian passport holders, the correct pathway depends on the purpose, duration and main destination. Getting this decision right matters more than submitting a bulky file.
For tourism, business meetings, conferences or family visits, the usual route is a Schengen Type C visa. It permits temporary travel across 29 countries, including France, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Norway, Bulgaria and Romania. The UK, Ireland and Cyprus are not covered.
The maximum stay is 90 days within any rolling 180-day period across the entire Schengen Area-not 90 days in every country. A multiple-entry visa allows repeated visits during its validity, but it does not change this limit or create a right to work.
Traveller’s visiting several countries must apply to their main destination, normally where they will spend the most days or pursue the principal purpose. If the stays are equal, apply to the first-entry country. An Indian legally resident in the UAE should normally apply there.
The standard visa fee is €90 for adults and €45 for children aged six to under 12, with visa-center charges added separately. Applications may be lodged up to six months before travel and, as a rule, no later than 15 days before departure. The normal decision period is 15 calendar days, although cases requiring further examination can take up to 45 days.
One widespread misconception concerns passport validity. The legal Schengen requirement is generally three months after the intended departure from Schengen, not six months after returning. The passport must also contain two blank pages and have been issued within the previous ten years.
Travel medical insurance must remain valid throughout Schengen for the complete trip and provide at least €30,000 of coverage for emergency treatment, hospitalization and repatriation.
There is no common Schengen-wide minimum bank balance. Each destination assesses whether the applicant can realistically afford the itinerary, accommodation and return journey. For a self-funded seven-to-ten-day trip, 8,000 EUROS to 10,000 EUROS may be a comfortable practical range for many applicants, but it is neither a legal threshold nor a guarantee.
Regular income, stable account activity and explainable funds are more convincing than money transferred shortly before applying. Employment, business, family responsibilities and previous lawful travel can also demonstrate reasons to return.
VFS Global or another authorized center may collect the application, supporting documents, biometrics and fees. It does not approve the visa. The consulate or competent national authority makes the decision, and premium processing-lounge services do not improve the merits of the case.
Study, employment, research, family reunification or relocation usually requires a national Type D visa and/or residence permit. Highly qualified professionals may qualify for an EU Blue Card, while students, founders and remote workers may have specialized national routes. One country’s residence permit does not automatically authorize work or residence throughout Europe.
The UK and Ireland operate separate immigration systems. A limited British-Irish Visa Scheme exception exists for certain Indian nationals living in India whose eligible visa is marked “BIVS”; UAE-based Indian residents should not assume that it applies. Cyprus should also be checked separately.
The EU Entry/Exit System became fully operational on 10 April 2026. Indian short-stay travellers now have their passport details, facial image, fingerprints and entry or exit recorded digitally at participating external borders. There is no advance EES application.
European Travel Information and Authorization System.
It is an online pre-travel authorization for people from countries that can enter Europe without a visa. It is similar to the US ESTA and is not a visa: it is intended for visa-exempt nationalities. For an Indian passport holder, ETIAS does not apply. Indians must obtain a Schengen visa, and they will not need ETIAS in addition even if they are UAE residents. At the border, however, their entry and biometric details are recorded through the separate Entry/Exit System (EES). Indian citizens travelling on a required Schengen visa will not need ETIAS in addition.
Ultimately, the strongest visa application is not the thickest. It is the one in which the purpose, itinerary, finances and intention to return tell one clear and credible story.
